page.layout: One page of text: running head at top; poem block with headings in the centre and verse lines; a second poem section below a rule; a catchword-like word "Obse" at the lower right is cut off by the edge (treated as a partial word, not a catchword). No marginal notes.

l.i: Quæ fuerant legum pulpita, nunc asinis.
Sint tua doctores, Lelii, qui exempla sequantur:
Clausa aperit Clavis, penetrat quaque obvia
Sic quot transfossus Clavis palmasque manusque
Ecce patet misero totidem ceu Clavibus orbi

main_text.l: In librum Poematum Clariss. V. I A

l.i: Lex quod amicitia, tua quod lectissima virtus
Conabar præstare tibi, quum noster Apollo
Ecquid, ait, furiose paras? Lucem addere Soli
Sic ille. At contra, ne me inquam, Phoebe, putato

page.notes: The first lines of the poem are partly damaged and read with [?] where uncertain; the lower-right word "Obse" is cut off at the edge. Long s has been normalised to s. The line "Lex quod amicitia" is a probable misreading of "Ex quod amicitia" in the scan and is uncertain; the opening capital L is a large initial.
